findings.title: Backup code reuse race condition
findings.body: In the authorize callback, backup code consumption is not atomic. The code reads the user's backupCodes, finds the code, sets it to null, and updates the DB. Two concurrent login requests using the same valid backup code can both read the same backupCodes array before either update commits, so both will pass the `indexOf` check and both log in. This defeats the one-time use guarantee of backup codes. Use a conditional update (e.g., updateMany with a filter on the backupCodes value, or a transaction with row lock) to ensure each code is consumed exactly once.

findings.title: Download button triggers form submission
findings.body: The download button is rendered inside the form as ``. The Button's default type is "submit" and there is no `onClick` handler that calls `preventDefault`. Clicking it will submit the surrounding form (which calls `handleEnable` with the still-registered `totpCode`), in addition to the anchor's download navigation. This can cause a second `/enable` API request after 2FA has already been enabled, producing an error or unintended side effects. The Button should have `type="button"` or an `onClick={(e) => e.preventDefault()}`.

findings.title: Backup code option not available for OAuth/SSO 2FA flow
findings.body: When `totpEmail` is present (i.e., the user is in the 2FA challenge after an OAuth/SSO login), the footer renders `ExternalTotpFooter`, which only contains a cancel button. There is no "Lost access" button to switch to the backup code input, even though the `authorize` callback in `next-auth-options.ts` supports backup codes for any user with `twoFactorEnabled`. Users who log in via Google/SAML and have 2FA enabled cannot use their backup codes if they lose access to their authenticator. The backup code option should be available in this flow as well.

findings.title: Component name is wrong
findings.body: The exported component is named `TwoFactor` although this file implements the backup code input field. This is misleading and may confuse maintainers. Rename it to `BackupCode` to match the file and usage.
